issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify lectureName as a String attribute, and the template expects students to add attributes accordingly. The solution implementation, however, declares lectureName as a LectureName object (custom class). This type mismatch affects the constructor parameter, getters/setters, and general usage of the lectureName attribute and will confuse students about the intended type.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the type of lectureName consistent across artifacts. Preferably change the solution to use a String for lectureName (update the field, constructor parameter, getters/setters, and toString accordingly) to match the UML and problem statement. Alternatively, if a LectureName wrapper is intended, update the problem statement and template to specify LectureName and adjust the getter/setter signatures and documentation accordingly.

issues.description: In the solution, getLectureName() is declared to return String but returns the lectureName field which is declared as LectureName. This causes a method return type mismatch and will lead to a compilation error or confusion about the expected return type of the getter.
issues.suggestedFix: Fix the getter signature or the field type so they match. Either change getLectureName() to return LectureName (and document that in the problem statement/template) or change the lectureName field to a String and return String from the getter. Ensure the template, problem statement, and solution all use the same return type.
